posts.text: Bitcoin Core is rewriting its security policy for a world where $BTC bugs can be found with a single AI prompt. The project will now backport fixes and cut releases immediately for flaws flagged as “easily discoverable,” moving away from the long embargoes that once gave developers time to patch quietly. The change targets a new threat model: attackers using AI to surface vulnerabilities quickly, before a slow disclosure process can contain them. Under the revised approach, easily discoverable bugs get fast-tracked fixes and releases rather than extended secrecy. That shift matters because embargoes are meant to protect users while a fix is prepared.
